questions.content: A random variable $X$ has probabilities $P(X=1)=0.1$, $P(X=2)=0.5$, $P(X=3)=0.2$, and an unknown $P(X=4)$. Find the missing probability, $E(X)$, and $\operatorname{Var}(X)$.

A drug's six-month profit contribution is USD -30,000 with probability 0.2, USD 50,000 with probability 0.5, and USD 200,000 with probability 0.3. Management will market the drug only if expected profit exceeds USD 90,000. Decide.
A lawyer has probability 0.3 of winning a case and earns USD 40,000 if she wins and nothing if she loses. She must spend USD 5,000 preparing the case in either outcome. Find her expected net gain.
A vaccine is 95% effective. For 20 independent individuals, find the probability that it is ineffective for exactly one individual.
A vaccine is 95% effective. For 20 independent individuals, find the probability that it is ineffective for more than one individual.

The probability that a reported residential-service problem is repaired the same day is 0.75. For the first five reported problems, find the mean and standard deviation of the number repaired the same day.

Thirty percent of a cleaning company's jobs finish within the bid time. For a random sample of 8 jobs, find the probability that the number finished on time is within one standard deviation of its mean.
A grocery-store service desk serves an average of 4 customers per half-hour. Assuming a Poisson distribution, find the probability that at most 2 customers use the desk in a half-hour.
A grocery-store service desk serves an average of 4 customers per half-hour. Assuming a Poisson process, find the probability that exactly 2 customers use the desk in a one-hour period.

State blood-program data claim that 40% of individuals have group A blood. In a random sample of 6, exactly 3 have group A blood. Using the one-sided probability $P(X\ge3)$ under $X\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(6,0.4)$, assess the claim.

A flight's actual time $X$, in minutes, is uniformly distributed on [120, 140] dollars.

a. Give the density.

b. Describe its graph.

c. Find $P(125\le X\le135)$.

d. Find the probability that a flight is at least 5 minutes late when the quoted time is 130 minutes.

For a population with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$, find the mean, variance, and standard deviation of the sampling distribution of $\bar X$ in each case.

a. $\mu=10$, $\sigma=2$, $n=25$

b. $\mu=3$, $\sigma=0.1$, $n=4$

c. $\mu=500$, $\sigma=0.5$, $n=100$

A bank's population waiting-time standard deviation is known to be $2.47$ minutes. For a random sample of 100 customers, $\bar x=5.46$. Investigate $H_0:\mu=6$ against $H_a:\mu<6$.

a. Describe the sampling distribution of $\bar X$.

b. Find its mean and standard deviation under $H_0$.

c. Find $P(\bar X\le5.46\mid\mu=6)$.

d. State the conclusion.

Use the rule $np\ge10$ and $n(1-p)\ge10$ to decide whether the sampling distribution of $\hat p$ can be treated as normal.

a. $p=0.4,n=100$

b. $p=0.1,n=10$

c. $p=0.1,n=50$

d. $p=0.8,n=400$

e. $p=0.98,n=1000$

f. $p=0.99,n=400$
A poll of 1,000 parents found $\hat p=0.17$ using V-chips. To test the claim $p<0.20$, assume $p=0.20$ and use a normal approximation to find $P(\hat p\le0.17)$.
In a random sample of 1,031 adults, $\hat p=0.42$ had vacationed for at least six days. To assess $H_0:p=0.40$ versus $H_a:p>0.40$, use a normal approximation to find $P(\hat p\ge0.42)$.

A spinner lands in regions A, B, C, and D with probabilities $4/12$, $3/12$, $1/12$, and $4/12$, respectively. Each game costs 4 dollars. Landing on B pays a 10-dollar bonus, landing on D pays a 0.10-dollar bonus, and A or C pays no bonus. Find the expected net payoff per game.
